headline.headline: PISTONS PUSH CAVALIERS TO THE BRINK, ONE WIN FROM CONFERENCE FINALS
headline.deck: Detroit's suffocating defense holds Cleveland to 82 points in a commanding Game 4 victory.
headline.body:
CLEVELAND — The Detroit Pistons arrived at Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse on Friday night and turned the Eastern Conference Semifinals into a rout, dismantling the Cleveland Cavaliers 95-82 in Game 4 to seize a commanding 3-1 series lead. One more win stands between a franchise that spent years in the lottery and a berth in the Eastern Conference Finals.

Detroit's defense was the story from tip-off, clamping down on Donovan Mitchell and holding the Cavaliers to their lowest scoring output of these playoffs. The Pistons rotated with purpose, collapsed on dribble penetration and contested every pull-up jumper Cleveland attempted, turning what had been a high-octane Cavaliers offense into a series of forced possessions and empty trips down the floor.

The Pistons now return home for Game 5 with a chance to close out the series in front of their own crowd. Detroit has not reached the conference finals since the 2008 postseason, and the franchise's long-suffering fanbase will pack Little Caesars Arena knowing their team is four quarters away from ending nearly two decades of waiting.

secondary.headline: GOLDEN KNIGHTS PAY THE PRICE: STRIPPED OF PICK, TORTORELLA FINED FOR MEDIA LOCKOUT
secondary.deck: NHL punishes Vegas ahead of conference finals clash with Colorado, sending a stern message.
secondary.body:
The NHL dropped a hammer on the Vegas Golden Knights on Friday, stripping the franchise of a second-round draft pick and fining head coach John Tortorella $100,000 after the team was found to have boxed out media from access it was entitled to under league rules. The punishment lands at a particularly uncomfortable moment, with Vegas preparing for a conference finals matchup against the Colorado Avalanche.

Tortorella, never shy about his disdain for the press, has now cost his organization a tangible asset in a league where draft capital matters deeply. The Golden Knights are a Cup contender this spring, but the front office will feel the sting of this penalty for years. The Avalanche-Golden Knights series shapes up as one of the most anticipated second-round matchups of the spring, and Vegas will need every advantage it can muster to topple Nathan MacKinnon and company.

secondary.headline: FORMER NFL LINEMAN JOSH MAURO DIED FROM FENTANYL, COCAINE AND ETHANOL OVERDOSE, REPORT SAYS
secondary.deck: Toxicology results confirm a fatal drug combination claimed the life of the defensive lineman.
secondary.body:
A toxicology report has confirmed that former NFL defensive lineman Josh Mauro died from an acute combination of fentanyl, cocaine and ethanol intoxication, according to reports released Friday. Mauro, who played for several NFL franchises over a career that included stints with the Oakland Raiders and New York Giants, was found dead earlier this year, and the cause of death had remained under investigation until the report's release.

Mauro's death adds a painful chapter to a growing list of tragedies linked to the fentanyl crisis that has cut through all corners of American life, including professional athletics. The NFL Players Association has repeatedly called for expanded mental health and substance abuse resources for current and former players, and Mauro's case will likely intensify that conversation as the league heads into its offseason program calendar.

secondary.headline: DODGERS' BLAKE SNELL OUT INDEFINITELY WITH LOOSE BODIES IN ELBOW
secondary.deck: Los Angeles's prized rotation absorbs another blow as Snell exits start, faces uncertain timeline.
secondary.body:
ANAHEIM — Blake Snell's second start of the 2026 season never happened. The Dodgers left-hander was a late scratch Friday night at Angel Stadium after loose bodies were discovered in his elbow, leaving Los Angeles without a definitive timeline for his return and raising fresh questions about the health of a rotation built to carry the franchise deep into October.

Snell, who signed with Los Angeles as one of the most coveted arms on the market, has now appeared in just one game this season. Loose bodies in the elbow can be managed conservatively or require surgical intervention depending on severity, and the Dodgers said only that the southpaw is out indefinitely. For a club that has leaned heavily on pitching depth to navigate a long season, the news is a significant setback and one that will force manager Dave Roberts to reshape his rotation plans through at least the coming weeks.

column.headline: DETROIT'S MOMENT IS REAL, AND THE REST OF THE EAST SHOULD BE WORRIED
column.body:
There was a time, not so long ago, when the Detroit Pistons were a punchline. Years of lottery picks, coaching carousels and false dawns had beaten the optimism out of a fanbase that remembered the Goin' To Work era with a bittersweet ache. That time appears to be over. What the Pistons are doing to the Cleveland Cavaliers in this series is not a fluke. It is a clinic in defensive identity, and it is being administered by a young team that no longer flinches under pressure.

The Eastern Conference Finals spot is not guaranteed yet, but Detroit is one win away, and the way this team is constructed, with length, athleticism and a defensive scheme that scrambles opposing offenses, they look capable of troubling anyone remaining in the bracket. If the Pistons close out Cleveland at home, the conversation around this franchise will change overnight. Not just for a week. For years.

story.headline: SEAGER SITS, SMITH HOSPITALIZED AS INJURY STORM BATTERS RANGERS HEADING INTO HOUSTON
story.deck: Texas limps into Minute Maid Park shorthanded as medical woes pile up for the Rangers
story.body:
The Texas Rangers arrived in Houston for a pivotal three-game series Friday looking more like a walking infirmary than a playoff contender. Slumping shortstop Corey Seager was scratched from the lineup for the opener against the Astros, and second baseman Josh Smith remained hospitalized after being diagnosed with viral meningitis, a condition doctors say will sideline him for at least a week. The twin absences gutted the heart of a Texas infield already scraping to stay competitive in the AL West.

Smith's situation carries far greater urgency than a simple stint on the injured list. Viral meningitis is no routine baseball injury, and the Rangers organization confirmed Saturday that the 26-year-old infielder will remain under hospital care as doctors monitor his condition. There is no timetable for his return to the field, and the club has not ruled out a longer absence depending on how treatment progresses.

Seager's absence, meanwhile, speaks to a separate and growing concern in Arlington. The two-time Silver Slugger has scuffled at the plate for weeks, and manager Bruce Bochy elected to give his franchise cornerstone a rest rather than let the slump deepen against Houston's pitching staff. The Rangers, already navigating a crowded and unforgiving AL West, can ill afford to lose ground to the Astros this weekend, but they will have to find it with a patchwork lineup until their walking wounded find their way back.

story.headline: PISTONS SUFFOCATE CAVALIERS, PULL WITHIN ONE WIN OF CONFERENCE FINALS
story.deck: Detroit's defense holds Cleveland to 82 points in a gritty Game 5 victory.
story.body:
CLEVELAND — The Detroit Pistons came to Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse and did what no one outside their locker room believed they could do. Leaning on a suffocating defensive effort that held the Cleveland Cavaliers to just 82 points, Detroit walked out of Cleveland with a 95-82 victory Friday night, pushing the second-round series to the brink and leaving the Cavaliers one loss away from an early summer.

Cleveland's offense, which had carved up opponents all season behind Donovan Mitchell and Darius Garland, looked hesitant and disjointed from the opening tip. Mitchell finished with 21 points but required 19 field-goal attempts to get there, a testament to the relentless ball pressure Detroit applied all night. Garland was even more frustrated, managing just 11 points on 4-of-14 shooting as the Pistons' guards stayed glued to him in pick-and-roll coverage that Cleveland simply could not solve.

For Detroit, the victory was a collective effort built on physicality and purpose. Cade Cunningham controlled the pace at both ends of the floor, finishing with 24 points and 9 assists while keeping turnovers to a minimum. The Pistons now return home to Little Caesars Arena for a potential series-clinching Game 6 on Sunday, where a franchise that has not reached the conference finals in nearly two decades will have a chance to change that story in front of its own crowd.

story.headline: GOLDEN KNIGHTS STRIPPED OF SECOND-ROUND PICK, TORTORELLA FINED $100K FOR MEDIA INCIDENT
story.deck: NHL drops hammer on Vegas before Avalanche series even begins
story.body:
The NHL levied severe punishment on the Vegas Golden Knights on Saturday, stripping the franchise of its second-round draft pick and fining head coach John Tortorella $100,000 after the team was found guilty of blocking media access in a manner the league deemed a serious violation of its press conduct standards. The sanctions arrive at the worst possible moment for Vegas, which opens its Western Conference Finals series against the Colorado Avalanche with the front office already distracted by organizational turmoil and a cloud hanging over Tortorella's bench leadership.

The Golden Knights, who reached this stage of the playoffs on the strength of their defensive structure and Tortorella's characteristically aggressive systems, now face Nathan MacKinnon, Mikko Rantanen and a Colorado squad that has looked dangerous through two playoff rounds. Vegas goaltender Adin Hill will need to be at his absolute best against an Avalanche power play that has been clicking at over 27 percent in these postseason. Cale Makar, meanwhile, gives Colorado a game-breaking defenseman unlike anything Vegas can counter on the blue line.

For Tortorella, the six-figure fine stings, but the forfeited pick represents a longer-term blow to a franchise already navigating a complicated roster and salary cap situation heading into the offseason. Golden Knights general manager Kelly McCrimmon declined to comment Saturday beyond a brief statement acknowledging the sanctions. The series tips off next week, and Vegas will need to compartmentalize fast if it hopes to silence questions about internal dysfunction and focus on stopping the defending-champion Avalanche from rolling back to the Stanley Cup Final.

story.headline: SHEDEUR SANDERS BATTLES FOR STARTING ROLE AS BROWNS ROOKIES REPORT TO BEREA
story.deck: Cleveland's first-round pick faces stiff competition as OTAs heat up in Ohio.
story.body:
BEREA, Ohio — Shedeur Sanders arrived at the Cleveland Browns' facility this week with the kind of pedigree that turns heads and the kind of pressure that breaks quarterbacks. Selected in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Colorado, Sanders is competing with veteran Joe Flacco and second-year signal-caller Dorian Thompson-Robinson for the starting job under center, and head coach Kevin Stefanski has made clear that no job is handed out in Berea.

The Browns overhauled their offensive line this offseason, signing guard Will Fries away from Indianapolis on a four-year deal worth $64 million and trading a third-round pick to the Tennessee Titans for veteran tackle Andre Dillard. General manager Andrew Berry called the moves essential to giving any Browns quarterback a legitimate chance to succeed, pointing to a 2025 season in which Cleveland allowed 52 sacks, the third-worst total in the AFC.

Across the league, May minicamp activity is revealing early storylines. In Dallas, CeeDee Lamb skipped voluntary OTAs for the second consecutive offseason amid a simmering contract dispute, while the San Francisco 49ers officially released linebacker Dre Greenlaw after he failed a physical following knee surgery. For Sanders, the noise outside Cleveland matters little. The son of Hall of Fame cornerback Deion Sanders is focused on learning Stefanski's West Coast system and, by all early accounts, impressing coaches with his footwork and pocket awareness during 11-on-11 drills.
